_comment: Which committed pool each chain should serve.
The chain stores a pool's Merkle ROOT; the leaves it commits to — token, weight, reference
price, card — live here. A database is therefore not a cache of chain state but the preimage
of an on-chain commitment: without it the backend can neither publish odds nor build the proof
that settles a draw. This file is what lets a fresh deployment rebuild that preimage without a
human running CLI steps, and the root on chain is what proves the rebuild is honest.
Chains absent from this list are simply not pool-seeded on boot. ethereum_sepolia is absent
because it still serves the v1 8-card pool, whose leaves are generated by seed-testnet.ts rather
than held in a pool file. Give it a pool file and an entry here and it joins the automatic path.
